- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above recent high or align with 10-day moving average.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for such cases.  
- If sentiment shows sharp reversal (e.g., from negative to positive within 3–5 days), model lags in adjusting — add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment influence to forecast adjustment.  
- In cases where true price drops sharply after a spike, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings, model tends to overreact — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast to reduce noise.
